title: Traditional Dress
subtitle: Beads, color, and identity
body: Murle traditional dress is known for its vivid beadwork, often arranged in intricate patterns that carry meaning beyond decoration. Colors and arrangements can signal age-set membership, marital status, or personal achievement.

Beaded collars, waistbands, and headpieces are typically crafted by hand and passed down or gifted during important life events such as initiation or marriage. Skilled beadworkers are highly respected members of the community.
While daily dress has evolved over time, traditional attire remains central to ceremonies, dances, and celebrations, serving as a visible thread connecting the present to the past.
Photographs and detailed descriptions of specific patterns will be added here as the archive grows.
